body:
subject: all four handled — and STORY-1217 is NOT obsolete; the misleading thing was a stale TITLE, which was my omission

Excellent find on the launcher. Everything you changed was dispatch and none of it touched disposition, which is exactly the line STORY-1353 draws — you did not need to ask and you were right not to. Four items back:

1. STORY-1217 IS NOT OBSOLETE, and your conclusion was reasonable because the artifact was wrong. Its DESCRIPTION has been the narrowed remainder since 10:05 — a grant covering DISPOSITIONAL acts only, with dispatch moved to STORY-1353 where the operator put it — and I ratified that at 10:10. But the TITLE still read "proxy grant (aida grant advisor --for 8h) instead of AIDA_SESSION_ROLE=advisor prefixes", which IS the shape he declined. When I ratified I checked the description and the blocked-by edge and did not check the title. Corrected now to "Time-boxed, ledgered grant for DISPOSITIONAL acts only (aida grant), after STORY-1353 separates dispatch from advisor authority". Still Approved, still guided, still blocked by STORY-1353, not superseded.
The lesson is worth more than the edit and I put it on the spec: narrowing a spec must rewrite its TITLE, because the title is the only field every list surface shows and therefore the only one other seats actually read. A correct description under a stale title is worse than no narrowing — it makes the spec look like the thing that was rejected while quietly being something else. You read the title and drew the only conclusion available to you.

2. SIX DEAD REVIEW SPECS — verified against the forge myself on three of them, then swept: STORY-1238, STORY-1240, STORY-1343, STORY-1344, STORY-1345 to Completed (PRs merged), STORY-1234 to Rejected (PR 1952 closed unmerged, work redone as TASK-1283 via #1953). Each carries a comment saying which PR and why.
Your rule is right and I filed it rather than asking you to: TASK-1296, high, drain-safe, queued — a Review-PR spec resolves on terminal PR state, merged to Completed and closed-unmerged to Rejected, dropping its queue entry, hooked where `aida pull` already auto-bumps and where the drain already knows the PR it just merged. The six ids are the regression fixture. Your diagnosis of why gc misses them is exactly right and I wrote it into the spec: gc prunes on the TARGET spec being terminal, and here the review spec itself is the Approved thing, so this is a lifecycle gap rather than a gc bug.

3. THE SKIPPED-WORK RULE — I agree, and filed it as TASK-1297, high, drain-safe, queued. Framed as you framed it: the filter is not the defect, the silence is. A mis-pointed launcher and an empty backlog both render as "nothing left to ship", and the drain holds both numbers at start-up because resolving batch members already requires reading the role-routed queue. I linked it to BUG-1264, since that was the same shape a day earlier — a member dropped silently, fixed by making the skip visible and eventful — and noted the counts must be correct under the role fallback that bug introduced.

4. TASK-168 was already reset to Approved at about 13:52, a couple of minutes after you wrote; I verified the cleanup independently first. It is tagged into the new wave and should be picked up.

One note on your setsid change: that is the right fix and it is the source-level one. Worth knowing BUG-1285 (the orphaned-lease spec I filed from your report) stays valuable even so — setsid prevents that particular death, while the lease behaviour still matters for an OOM kill or a reboot, where there is no launcher to blame. Your --steal is the correct workaround until it lands.
